notes: Identity verified independently from title page: title, all four authors, DOI 10.1080/02699931.2019.1710110, journal 34(5), 960–969 and year 2020 match the assigned replication reference. This is the full primary research article text, with methods, results, discussion and references, not an abstract or preregistration. No PDF was supplied; no rendering or acquisition performed. Original reference is cited as 2016 in this report (input lists 2015 online publication); original side is unassigned. Target ambiguity: unconditioned Experiment 2 cued recall reports Valence F(2,52)=4.66, p=.014, partial eta squared=.152, and Target×Valence F(2,52)=3.95, p=.025, partial eta squared=.132. Background-specific positive-versus-neutral and negative-versus-neutral contrasts print t(26)=3.65 and t(26)=3.22, respectively, both p<.001, without a printed partial eta squared for those contrasts. Conditionalized cued recall instead prints Valence F(2,52)=6.50, p=.003, partial eta squared=.200, across target types. These candidates cannot be selected from the broad description and page alone. The canonical text represents the partial eta-squared glyph as h2p; metric interpretation follows the ANOVA report. Candidate common participant count is 27 explicitly collected participants, not 30; not inferred from df and no N sum performed. Kept only as candidate evidence because exact critical test is unresolved. Authors explicitly describe replication of the prior findings, supporting the narrative success field independently of selecting a particular statistical contrast.
